summary:
Every rating is running the same script right now, and that's the headline: R1 through R4 are all 3-1 (75%) over the last 14 days across trends, runs, sp, bullpen, and hitting, with sp carrying a 3-game win streak across the board. But bullpen_fatigue is a disaster everywhere — 0-4 (0%) with a 5-game losing streak on every single rating. That's not noise, that's a category to actively fade today. If a pick is only supported by bullpen_fatigue and nothing else, treat it as a red flag rather than a green light. The strong-play ledger backs up the hot streak: R2's 30-day window is 7-3 (70%, +3.0u) and R3 sits at 67% over the same stretch, both well ahead of their season paces, which tells you the model's recent sharpness isn't a fluke concentrated in one rating — it's systemic right now.

For today's slate, lean into the combos that are proven agreement signals: trends+sp (58%, 370-268) and trends+runs (57.3%, 404-301) are your top category pairs, and with sp riding a 3W streak across every rating, any game where trends and sp line up on the same side is the sharpest signal on the board. Cross-reference that against the team leaders — MIL (69%, n=74), TBR (70%, n=63), BOS (70%, n=56), and especially LAD, whose strong plays are hitting 80% (28-7, +27.0u) this season. If any of those four show up on tonight's card with trends+sp agreement, that's about as clean a stack as this model produces. Steer clear of NYY regardless of rating alignment — 49% overall and a brutal 39% (9-14, -4.0u) on strong plays makes it the one team where the model's own conviction has been a trap. With all four ratings moving in lockstep, there's no diversification benefit in splitting bets across R1-R4 today — the differentiator is category and team selection, not which rating number you're reading.
